description.value: This study used structural MRI to compare cortical gray matter volumes in treatment-naive heavy drinkers meeting criteria for alcohol dependence with light drinkers, and examined associations of cortical gray matter volume with age and lifetime duration of alcohol use.

spans.text: Structural MRI was used to assess whole brain and regional volumes of cortical gray matter and white matter in 24 young to middle-aged treatment-naive alcohol dependent males versus 17 controls.

description.value: Observational comparison of community-recruited heavy and light drinkers; no intervention was administered.

value: Heavy drinkers showed reduced total cortical gray matter and reduced posterior prefrontal, dorsolateral prefrontal, lateral parietal, and mesial parietal cortex compared with light drinkers; sulcal CSF was increased in all regions of reduced gray matter.
These findings indicate cortical gray matter volume reductions, primarily in prefrontal and parietal regions, in treatment-naive alcohol-dependent individuals.
